misconceptions.description: Adding force magnitudes as if they were scalars without resolving into components
misconceptions.trigger: learner reports the resultant of two non-collinear forces as the sum of their magnitudes
misconceptions.feedback: Forces have direction. Add them by components or by the parallelogram rule. Magnitudes only sum when the forces are collinear and in the same direction.

misconceptions.description: Building the unit vector along a line by normalizing one endpoint's position vector instead of the line's position vector
misconceptions.trigger: learner divides one endpoint coordinates by their magnitude to obtain a 'unit vector along the line'
misconceptions.feedback: The unit vector along a line from A to B uses r_AB = B - A, not A or B alone. The line is the difference of the two position vectors.

misconceptions.description: Treating the projection of a force onto an axis as the full force magnitude regardless of angle
misconceptions.trigger: learner reports F·u = |F| even when F and u are not parallel
misconceptions.feedback: F · u = |F||u|cosθ. Only when F is parallel to u (θ = 0) does the projection equal |F|. At other angles the projection is smaller.

misconceptions.description: Treating the cross product as commutative like the dot product
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes M = F × r instead of M = r × F (or vice versa) without noting the sign change
misconceptions.feedback: The cross product is anti-commutative: A × B = -B × A. For moments use M = r × F where r runs from the moment point to any point on F's line of action.
